questions.prompt: Queries/keys have d_k=256 with unit-variance independent entries. What is the standard deviation of q·k before scaling? (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
Scores (0, 0, ln 3) pass through softmax. What is the weight on the third key? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Self-attention, d_k=2, X=[(1,0),(0,1)], Q=K=V=X. What is output component 1 of token 1? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
questions.explanation: Weights (0.6698, 0.3302) on values (1,0),(0,1): first component is 0.6698.

questions.prompt: Three tokens all have equal scores and a causal mask is used. What weight does token 3 give to token 1? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Which implementation of a causal mask is correct?
options: weights computed first, then V rows for j > i deleted
scores[i][j] = -inf for j > i, then softmax
weights[i][j] = 0 for j > i after softmax, without renormalizing
scores[i][j] = 0 for j > i, then softmax
questions.explanation: Only -inf before softmax gives exact zeros and a normalized row.

questions.prompt: Sequence length goes from 256 to 1024. By what factor does the number of attention-weight entries per head grow? (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
Sinusoidal positional encoding with d=2: PE(pos) = (sin(pos), cos(pos)). What is the first component at pos=2? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
A model with no positional encoding is given 'robot avoids obstacle' and 'obstacle avoids robot'. What is true of its attention outputs for each word?
options: The model errors out on repeated tokens
Each word's output is the same in both sentences
Only the first word's output is the same
The outputs differ because the word order differs
questions.explanation: Same tokens, same set of query/key/value rows; without positions the per-token outputs do not depend on order.

questions.prompt: Tokenizing a rare word with BPE usually results in...
options: Several subword tokens from the vocabulary
An unknown-word token that discards the word
questions.explanation: Merges are learned from frequent strings, so rare words fall back to pieces; no unknown token is needed.
